exercise.title: Add9: the 2nd on top of the chord
exercise.why: An add9 chord keeps its 3rd and adds the 2nd on top, so it still sounds major, where a sus2 chord gives the 3rd up.

cells.text:
Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} on the staff below: a C major chord, one note at a time. Tap them again and add the ringed {{2}} from the octave above: that is Cadd9.
The added note is called the 9 because it is the 2nd counted on past the octave.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Go from C to Cadd9, then from C to Csus2: in add9 the 3rd is still there, in sus2 it is gone.
Practice until you can tell which of the two still sounds major.

This staff builds the same chord from another root. Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}}, then add the ringed {{2}} from the octave above.
Once you can hum the added note before you tap it, try another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key.
When you change the key, the notes are new but the added note is still the {{2}}, an octave up.
